note: Notes for translators, by English text. `node scripts/i18n.js extract` copies each into lang/en.json next to its text. See lang/README.md.

notes.Day: Bottom tab: the log of one day. Also the 'Day' column of the stats table and a screen name in the report form. One short word.
notes.Month: Bottom tab: the calendar of a month. One short word.
notes.Stats: Bottom tab: statistics and charts. One short word (a usual abbreviation is fine).
notes.Guide: Bottom tab: the baby-care guide (common worries, milestones, medicines). One short word.
notes.Family: Bottom tab: family sharing (who can see and add to the log). One short word.
notes.More: Bottom tab: settings and everything else. Also the Day page's button for the other kinds of entry. One short word.
notes.Children: Spoken label (screen readers) of the row of buttons that switches between children.
notes.Show me around this screen: Spoken label of the ❓ button that starts a short guided tour of the screen.
notes.Feeding: Heading of the group of feeds (breast or bottle) in the day's log.
notes.Diapers: Heading of the group of diaper (nappy) changes in the day's log, and of a stats card.
notes.Vomit: Heading of the group of times the baby was sick (vomited); also the label of the button that logs one.
notes.Play: Heading of the group of play times; the button that logs one; and one kind of play (general playing).
notes.Health & meds: Heading of the group of health notes and medicines given.
notes.Feed: Noun: one feed (breastfeed or bottle). Label of the button that logs one. Not the same word as Meal (an older child's meal): a page can show both.
notes.Diaper: Noun: one diaper (nappy) change. Label of the button that logs one, and an answer to 'Why did the baby wake?' (a wet or dirty diaper).
notes.Sleep: Noun: one sleep (nap or night sleep). Label of the button that logs one, and a stats card.
notes.Night wake: Noun: one time the baby woke in the night. Label of the button that logs one.
notes.Health: Label of the button that logs a health note (symptoms, temperature).
notes.Meds: Short for medicines: label of the button that logs a medicine or vitamin given.
notes.feed: Lower-case noun for one entry, only used in the titles 'Add {what}' and 'Edit {what}': give the form that fits there (for example the accusative).
notes.diaper: Lower-case noun for one entry, only used in the titles 'Add {what}' and 'Edit {what}': give the form that fits there.
notes.sleep: Lower-case noun for one entry, only used in the titles 'Add {what}' and 'Edit {what}': give the form that fits there.
notes.night wake: Lower-case noun for one entry, only used in the titles 'Add {what}' and 'Edit {what}': give the form that fits there.
notes.vomit: Lower-case noun for one entry (a time the baby was sick), only used in the titles 'Add {what}' and 'Edit {what}'.
notes.play: Lower-case noun for one entry (a play time), only used in the titles 'Add {what}' and 'Edit {what}'.
notes.health note: Lower-case noun for one entry, only used in the titles 'Add {what}' and 'Edit {what}'.
notes.meds: Lower-case noun for one entry (a medicine given), only used in the titles 'Add {what}' and 'Edit {what}'.
notes.Add {what}: Title of the form for a new entry. {what} is one of: feed, diaper, sleep, night wake, vomit, play, health note, meds (translated).
notes.Edit {what}: Title of the form for changing an entry. {what} is one of: feed, diaper, sleep, night wake, vomit, play, health note, meds (translated).
notes.Entry: One item in the log (a feed, a diaper change …), used when its kind is unknown.
notes.Rash: A symptom ticked in a health note.
notes.Fever: A symptom ticked in a health note.
notes.rash: Diaper rash, added after the diaper contents: 'Pee, rash'.
notes.Red-streaked: Colour of the baby's poo (stool): with streaks of red (blood).
notes.Tummy time: A kind of play: time the baby spends lying on their tummy while awake.
notes.Skin-to-skin: A kind of play: the baby held against a parent's bare chest.
notes.Bath: A kind of play: bath time.
notes.Hungry: An answer to 'Why did the baby wake in the night?'.
notes.Gas / fussy: An answer to 'Why did the baby wake in the night?': wind, or unsettled.
notes.Unknown: An answer to 'Why did the baby wake in the night?': no idea.
notes.Why?: Why the baby woke in the night (answers: Hungry, Diaper, Gas / fussy, Unknown).
notes.Both: Breast side for a breastfeed: both breasts.
notes.Side: Which breast the baby fed from (Left, Right, Both).
notes.Breast milk: What was in the bottle: expressed breast milk.
notes.Formula: What was in the bottle: infant formula (formula milk).
notes.Formula name: Spoken label of the field for the brand of infant formula.
notes.Usual formula: The brand of infant formula a child usually has (settings).
notes.Choose a formula…: Button that opens the list of infant formula brands.
notes.Spit-up: How much the baby brought up: a small amount of milk (a posset). Also the label of the quick button for that.
notes.Medium: How much the baby vomited: a medium amount.
notes.Large: How much the baby vomited: a large amount.
notes.small: How much the baby vomited (old entries): a small amount. Shown in 'Vomit – {amount}'.
notes.Vomit – {amount}: {amount} is how much: Spit-up, Medium, Large or small (translated).
notes.projectile: Projectile vomiting (forceful), shown under a vomit entry.
notes.Projectile: Projectile vomiting (forceful): a checkbox in the vomit form.
notes.A little: Quick button: the baby brought up a little milk.
notes.More than usual: Quick button: the baby was sick more than usual.
notes.breast: Kind of feed in the feed form: breastfeed.
notes.bottle: Kind of feed in the feed form: bottle feed.
notes.Pee: Diaper contents: wet (urine). Also what a child did on the potty, so a word that fits both.
notes.Poo: Diaper contents: dirty (stool), and what a child did on the potty, so a word that fits both. Friendly, informal word.
notes.Pee + Poo: Diaper contents, or what a child did on the potty: both.
notes.Dry: Diaper contents: dry, nothing in it.
notes.pee: Series name in a chart of diapers per day: wet diapers.
notes.poo: Series name in a chart of diapers per day: dirty diapers.
notes.{pee} pee, {poo} poo: Counts of wet and dirty diapers in a day: '5 pee, 2 poo'.
notes.Poo colours: Stats: how often each poo colour was seen.
notes.Poop colours: Guide topic: what the colours of a baby's poo mean.
notes.{m}m: Minutes, as in '45m' (durations). Use the usual short form for minutes.
notes.{h}h {m}m: Hours and minutes, as in '1h 20m' (durations). Use the usual short forms.
notes.{h}h: Hours, as in '2h' (durations), also chart values like '9.5h'.
notes.{n} ml: Millilitres of milk, as in '90 ml'.
notes.{n} feed: Milk feeds (breast or bottle) in a day, in the summary under the feeding heading; meals of solid food are counted after it, as 'Solids ×2'.
notes.ml: Millilitres, the unit of bottle feeds (chart series name).
notes.until {time}: {time} is a clock time, as in '14:30'.
notes.Awake {n} min: A night waking that lasted {n} minutes.
notes.Awake: A night waking (the baby was awake).
notes.Temp {t}°: Temperature: {t} is a number, as in 'Temp 37.8°'.
notes.Trip {by}: {by} is how: 'by car', 'by plane', 'by train' or 'by ship' (translated).
notes.Travelling {by}: {by} is how: 'by car', 'by plane', 'by train' or 'by ship' (translated).
notes.under way: The current part of a journey is still going on.
notes.travelling: Spoken label of a calendar day when the family was away travelling.
notes.Baby {n}: Name used for a child without a name yet: 'Baby 2'.
notes.{name}'s Log: Title at the top: '{name}' is the child's name ('Ava's Log').
notes.Everyone: Title when the log of all children is shown together.
notes.All: Button that shows all children together.
notes.24 h: Clock face showing the whole day (24 hours). Short.
notes.12 h: Clock face showing half a day (12 hours). Short.
notes.AM: The morning half of a 12-hour clock (button). Short.
notes.PM: The afternoon/evening half of a 12-hour clock (button). Short.
Written small in the middle of the clock face when it shows the morning half.
Written small in the middle of the clock face when it shows the afternoon/evening half.
notes.Half of the day: Spoken label of the AM / PM buttons.
notes.Clock face: Spoken label of the 24 h / 12 h buttons.
notes.Clock art: The picture behind the clock (a painting or pattern), chosen by the parent.
notes.Whole day: Button that goes back from one part of the day to the whole day.
notes.Night: A quarter of the day on the clock (about midnight to 6:00), or of the evening half (about 21:00 to midnight).
notes.Morning: A quarter of the day on the clock.
notes.Afternoon: A quarter of the day on the clock.
notes.Evening: A quarter of the day on the clock.
notes.{group}: {n}: Spoken summary of the clock: '{group}' is a group such as Feeding, {n} a count.
notes.{clock}: {entries}: Spoken summary of the clock: '{clock}' names the clock, '{entries}' lists the counts.
notes.day {n}: Day number of a trip, as in 'Trip by car · day 3'.
notes.Numbers: Opens a table of the numbers behind a chart.
notes.feeds: Series name in a chart: feeds per day.
notes.vomits: Series name in a chart: times sick per day.
notes.hours asleep: Series name in a chart: hours of sleep per day.
notes.night wakings: Series name in a chart: night wakings per day.
notes.none: Stats: no health notes in the period.
notes.{what} per day, last {n} day: Spoken label of a chart. {what} lists the series ('feeds and ml'); {n} the number of days.
notes.Pediatrician: The child's own doctor (paediatrician or family doctor).
notes.Practice: Field: the name of the doctor's practice (clinic, surgery).
notes.After hours / nurse line: Field: the phone number to call out of hours, or a nurse advice line.
notes.Emergency?: Bold start of the line saying when to call the emergency number.
notes.Right now: Guide: what is common at the child's age right now.
notes.Around {age}:: {age} is an age such as '2 months' (translated).
notes.Checkup: A routine check-up with the doctor at a given age.
notes.UK: {age}: When the same check-up happens in the UK; {age} as in '6–8 weeks'.
notes.US: {age}: When the same check-up happens in the US; {age} as in '2 months'.
notes.Pictures: Guide: opens the pictures (photos or drawings) of a condition. They are hidden until opened.
notes.Picture credits: Who made each picture and its licence.
notes.From: Picture credits: 'From <web address>' (where the picture came from).
notes.photo by {by}, {licence}: Picture credits: {by} is a person's name, {licence} a licence such as 'CC BY-SA 4.0'.
notes.drawing by {by}, {licence}: Picture credits: {by} is a person's name, {licence} a licence such as 'CC BY-SA 4.0'.
notes.cropped: Picture credits: the picture was cropped.
notes.cropped and resized: Picture credits: the picture was cropped and made smaller.
notes.Soft spots: Guide topic: the fontanelles on a baby's head.
notes.Milia: Guide topic: tiny white spots on a newborn's nose and cheeks (milia).
notes.Cradle cap: Guide topic: scaly patches on a baby's scalp (seborrhoeic dermatitis).
notes.Meconium: Guide: a newborn's first, dark, sticky poo.
notes.Gripe water: An over-the-counter remedy for colic. Keep as it is known locally.
notes.Acetaminophen (paracetamol): The pain and fever medicine (acetaminophen in the US, paracetamol elsewhere). Use the name people know locally; keeping both names is fine.
notes.Change trip: Button: change the dates or the travel mode of a trip.
notes.We're home: Button: the trip is over, the family is back home.
notes.Travelling?: Bold start of the button that starts travel mode.
notes.Asleep: Quick button in travel mode: the baby fell asleep.
notes.Leaving: Date field: the day the trip starts.
notes.Back home: Date field: the day the family comes home.
notes.Just today: Length of a trip: just today.
notes.Plan it: Button: save a trip that starts on a later day.
notes.Car: A means of travel (trip by car).
notes.Plane: A means of travel (trip by plane).
notes.Train: A means of travel (trip by train).
notes.Ship: A means of travel (trip by ship or ferry).
notes.Set off: Button on a car journey: we have started driving.
notes.Taking off: Button on a flight: the plane is taking off.
notes.Landed: Button on a flight: the plane has landed.
notes.Boarded: Button on a train journey: we got on the train.
notes.Got off: Button on a train journey: we got off the train.
notes.Set sail: Button on a sea journey: the ship has left.
notes.Docked: Button on a sea journey: the ship has arrived.
notes.At sea: A part of a sea journey: sailing.
notes.In port: A part of a sea journey: stopped in a port.
notes.Road trip: Name of a clock picture used when travelling by car.
notes.By train: Name of a clock picture used when travelling by train.
notes.Gilt classic: Name of a clock picture: a classic gold-framed clock.
notes.Other days: Tour step title: the arrows that go to earlier days.
notes.Every detail: Tour step title: the groups of entries below the clock.
notes.Everything else: Tour step title: the tabs at the bottom.
notes.The journey: Tour step title: the buttons for the parts of a journey.
notes.The rest: Tour step title: the less common kinds of entry, one more tap away.
notes.Next: Tour: go to the next step.
notes.Back: Tour: go to the previous step.
notes.Done: Button: finish (the tour, or close a window).
notes.When?: When it happened (Just now, about 15 min ago …).
notes.~{n} min ago: When it happened: about {n} minutes ago.
notes.~1 hr ago: When it happened: about an hour ago.
notes.Tap one to save: Above the quick buttons: tapping one saves the entry straight away.
notes.Fell asleep: Title of the quick form that logs the start of a sleep.
notes.Woke up: Button: the baby woke up (ends the sleep).
notes.tap to set wake time: Under a sleep that has not ended: tap it to say when the baby woke.
notes.Signing in: A screen name in the language report form: the sign-in screens.
notes.Somewhere else: A screen name in the language report form: another place in the app.
notes.Automatic: {region}: Setting that follows the phone: {region} is the country or region found (translated by the phone).
notes.Automatic: {language}: Language setting that follows the phone: {language} is the language found.
notes.Match phone: Appearance: light or dark, the same as the phone.
notes.Sunrise & sunset: Appearance: light by day, dark at night, by the sun where you are.
notes.Backup (JSON): Button: save a backup file (JSON is a file type; keep it).
notes.Export CSV: Button: save the log as a spreadsheet file (CSV is a file type; keep it).
notes.Type: Kind of feed (breast, bottle or solids) in the feed form; also a column of the spreadsheet (CSV) export: the kind of entry. A general word for 'type' or 'kind'.
notes.Minutes: How long the breastfeed lasted, in minutes.
notes.Amount (ml): How much milk was in the bottle, in millilitres.
notes.Milk: What was in the bottle or cup: breast milk, formula, cow's milk… From a year old it is also the name of the entry and its button (a drink of milk). One short word.
notes.Poo colour: The colour of the baby's poo (stool).
notes.Now: Button: set the time to now.
notes.e.g. 15: Example in an empty field (minutes). Keep the number.
notes.e.g. 90: Example in an empty field (millilitres). Keep the number.
notes.e.g. 20: Example in an empty field (minutes). Keep the number.
notes.e.g. 10: Example in an empty field (minutes). Keep the number.
notes.e.g. 1 ml: Example in an empty field: a dose. Keep the number and unit.
notes.e.g. Vitamin D: Example in an empty field: a medicine or vitamin.
notes.e.g. Mum: Example in an empty field: what the baby calls you (a family name such as Mum, Dad, Grandma).
notes.optional: Example in an empty field: it may be left empty.
notes.Temperature (°): Body temperature in degrees (whatever unit the parent uses).
notes.For: Which children the entry is for.
notes.Deleted: Message after an entry is deleted.
notes.Removed: Message after a child is removed.
notes.Other: Another formula, not in the list.
notes.Name: The child's name.
notes.Not set: The child's sex has not been given.
notes.Colour: The child's colour in the app (to tell children apart).
notes.Baby: A child without a name (used as a name). Also the stage of life from 3 to 12 months, a heading in the journal of big moments.
notes.someone else: Used as a name: 'You can't change entries added by someone else'.
notes.Add entries: A permission: may add entries to the log.
notes.Parent: A role in the family log: full control.
notes.Family member: A role in the family log.
notes.Caregiver: A role in the family log: a nanny or other carer.
notes.Babysitter: A role in the family log.
notes.Friend: A role in the family log.
notes.Member: A role whose name is not known.
notes.Role: The role of a person in the family log (Parent, Family member, Caregiver, Babysitter, Friend).
notes.{actor} created a {role} invite: Activity log. {actor} is a person's name, {role} a role (Parent, Friend …, translated). Reword freely, e.g. 'created an invite for a {role}'.
notes.{actor} rescinded a {role} invite: Activity log. {actor} is a person's name, {role} a role. Rescinded = cancelled.
notes.{email} asked to join as {role}: Activity log. {email} is an email address, {role} a role.
notes.{actor} approved {email} as {role}: Activity log. {actor} is a person's name, {email} an email address, {role} a role.
notes.{actor} made {person} a {role}: Activity log. {actor} and {person} are people's names, {role} a role.
notes.just now: When something last happened: just now (used in 'Synced {when}').
notes.{time} ago: {time} is a duration such as '5m' or '2h 10m'. Also used in 'Synced {when}'.
notes.expires in {time}: An invite: {time} is a duration such as '2h 10m'.
notes.Android phone: The kind of a device joined to the log.
notes.Web browser: The kind of a device joined to the log: the app in a web browser.
notes.phone: The kind of a device joined to the log, when not known.
notes.you: Used as a name, for the person using this phone: 'added by you'.
notes.(you): After your own name in the list of people.
notes.(this phone): After the name of the phone you are using, in the list of phones.
notes.added {date}: When a phone was added: {date} is a date.
notes.Code: The sign-in code sent by email.
notes.you@example.com: Example in the email field. Keep it exactly as it is.
notes.Different email: Button: use a different email address to sign in.
notes.Two-step verification: Extra sign-in check with an authenticator app (two-factor authentication).
notes.Copy key: Button: copy the setup key of the authenticator app.
notes.Create log: Button: create a new family log (the shared diary of the baby).
notes.Send request: Button: ask to join a family log.
notes.Check now: Button: check whether the request to join has been approved.
notes.Check again: Button: check again whether this phone has been approved.
notes.You're in!: Message: your request to join the family log was approved.
notes.Share…: Button: share the code with another app (messages, email …).
notes.It matches: Checkbox: the security code they read out matches the one shown.
notes.Security code: A code two phones compare to check they are talking to each other securely.
notes.Deny: Button: do not let this person join.
notes.Approve phone: Button: let this phone see the family log (it gets the encryption keys).
notes.My phones: The phones (and browsers) signed in to your account.
notes.Open invites: Invites that have not been used yet.
notes.Show: Button: show (an invite code, or another child's log).
notes.Showing: Shown next to the child whose log is open.
notes.Relationship: Field: how this person is related to the child (grandparent, nanny …).
notes.Place of work: Field: where this person works (to reach them).
notes.Work phone: Field: the person's work phone number.
notes.Change access: Button: change this person's role and permissions.
notes.Reset: Message: two-step verification was reset for that person.
notes.Activity: A kind of entry and its button for a school child: an activity (sport, swimming, dance, music, a club…), and the label of the field in the play form (which kind of play or activity). Not the log of changes (that is 'Activity log').
notes.On (required for parents): Two-step verification is on, and parents must have it.
notes.App lock: Locking the app with the phone's fingerprint, face or passcode.
notes.Lock after: How soon the app locks after you leave it.
notes.Use passcode: Button on the phone's fingerprint or face prompt: use the phone's passcode instead.
notes.Connected: Cloud backup: connected to this service.
notes.Not connected: Cloud backup: not connected to this service.
notes.Back up: Button: save a backup to the cloud service now (verb).
notes.Restore: Button: bring back the log from the backup.
notes.Connect: Button: connect a cloud service (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive).
notes.Disconnect {service}: Spoken label of the ✕ button: {service} is Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive.
notes.Cloud backup: Encrypted backups to Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive.
notes.Save passphrase: Button: save the passphrase that encrypts the backups.
notes.Generate one: Button: make up a strong passphrase.
notes.Google Drive lookup: Inserted as {what} in '{what} failed ({status})': looking for the backup file.
notes.{what} failed ({status}): Error: {what} is what failed (for example 'Dropbox upload'), {status} an error number.
notes.Network timeout: Error: the internet connection took too long.
notes.Turned off: Message: a setting was turned off.
notes.Child: Which child: a column of the spreadsheet export, and a choice in the PDF report form.
notes.Date: Column heading: the date (in the spreadsheet export and the PDF report).
notes.Summary: Column of the spreadsheet (CSV) export: the entry in short, such as 'Bottle 90 ml'.
notes.Details: Heading of the day's entries below the clock; also a column of the spreadsheet (CSV) export.
notes.End: Column of the spreadsheet (CSV) export: when the entry ended (the end of a sleep).
notes.Note: A health note with no symptoms ticked; also a column of the spreadsheet (CSV) export (the note written with an entry).
notes.Routine: Bottom tab: the baby's daily routine (the times of day that repeat). One short word.
notes.Nap: A daytime sleep in the routine.
notes.Night sleep: The night's sleep in the routine (it starts in the evening or at night).
notes.until about {time} ({long}): A sleep in the routine: {time} is the clock time it usually ends, {long} how long it lasts, as in 'until about 11:15 (1h 45m)'.
notes.usually {from} – {to}: The clock times something in the routine happened on different days, as in 'usually 7:45 – 8:20'.
notes.{days} of {n} day: How often something in the routine happened: on {days} of the {n} days that were logged, as in '6 of 7 days'. The plural form goes with {n}.
notes.tomorrow at about {time}: When the next thing in the routine is: {time} is a clock time.
notes.about now ({time}): The next thing in the routine is due about now; {time} is its usual clock time.
notes.at about {time}, in {wait}: When the next thing in the routine is: {time} is a clock time, {wait} how long until then, as in '40m'.
notes.Done today at {time}: Spoken label of the tick next to a routine time: when it was logged today.
notes.Due now: Badge on the routine time that is happening about now.
notes.Up next: Badge on the next routine time today (not the 'Next' button of the tour).
notes.Not logged today: Spoken label: this routine time has passed today with nothing logged.
notes.Worked out from the last {days} days: fe: How the routine is found. {days} and {minutes} are numbers (7 and 45).
How many of the last 7 days have anything logged.
notes.Born {date}: PDF report: the child's date of birth, as in 'Born 24 August 2026'.
notes.{age} old: PDF report: the child's age; {age} is like '2 months' or '6 weeks' (translated).
notes.{from} to {to}: PDF report: the dates it covers; {from} and {to} are dates.
notes.At a glance: Heading in the PDF report: the averages.
notes.Day by day: Heading in the PDF report: a table with one row per day.
notes.Nothing logged: A day with no entries, in the PDF report's table.
notes.Highest temperature: PDF report: the highest temperature logged in the period.
notes.Symptoms noted: PDF report: the symptoms ticked in health notes, with how often.
notes.Medicines given: PDF report: the medicines given, with how often.
notes.Made with Little Log on {date}. Entries: Last line of the PDF report; {date} is today's date.
notes.{name}: report for the doctor: The title of the PDF; {name} is the child's name.
notes.Page {n} of {total}: At the bottom of each page of the PDF.
notes.Report for the doctor: Title of the form that makes a PDF of the log for the doctor (pediatrician).
notes.Report for the doctor (PDF): Button that opens the form for the PDF report for the doctor.
notes.Making the PDF…: Shown on the button while the PDF is being made.
notes.Include every entry: Checkbox: put every single entry in the PDF, not only the summaries.
notes.Numbers on the clock: Spoken label of the switch between Roman numerals (XII) and ordinary numbers (12) on the clock face.
notes.Roman numerals: One kind of numbers on the clock face (spoken label of its button, which shows XII).
notes.Easy-to-read numbers: The other kind: ordinary numbers 1 to 12 (spoken label of its button, which shows 123).
notes.Show in the list: Button: scroll down to this entry in the list below the clock, where it can be changed.
notes.To change or delete it, tap it in the li: In the sheet that shows an entry tapped on the clock.
notes.App updates: Heading in More: the card with the Update app button.
notes.Update app: Button: opens the app's page in the app store (Google Play or the App Store), where the update is installed.
notes.Version {version}: {version} is the app's version number, as in '1.2 (14)'.
notes.For the doctor: Tour step title: the button that makes a PDF for the doctor.
notes.It keeps up by itself: Tour step title: the routine updates by itself.
notes.Solids: A baby's meal of solid food (not breast milk or formula); an entry is shown as 'Solids: Banana, Peas'. Not the same word as Meal (an older child's meal).
notes.Solid meals per day: A row in Stats and in the doctor's report, next to 'Feeds per day' (which now counts milk feeds only): the average number of meals of solid food a day.
notes.solids: Kind of feed in the feed form, next to 'breast' and 'bottle': solid food.
notes.Food: Heading in the Guide: the section about starting solid foods.
notes.Foods: The twirl-down in the feed form with the foods to choose from.
notes.key allergen: Small label on a food that is one of the common allergens (peanut, egg …), best given early and often.
notes.allergy: Small label on a food the child is allergic to.
notes.Add: Button: add the food typed next to it.
notes.Allergies: {foods}: {foods} lists foods, as in 'Peanut, Egg' (each child's name comes first when there are several).
notes.first allergic reaction: {foods}: Spoken label of a calendar day; {foods} is a food or a list of foods.
notes.First allergic reaction: {foods}: On the day of a first allergic reaction; {foods} is a food.
notes.First allergic reaction: Calendar legend: the mark on the day of a first allergic reaction.
notes.first reaction {date}: {date} is a date, as in '3 March 2027'.
notes.Squash: A first food: butternut squash or pumpkin.
notes.Baby cereal: A first food: iron-fortified infant cereal.
notes.Tree nuts: A key allergen: almonds, cashews, walnuts … (ground, or as nut butter, for babies).
notes.Yogurt: A first food; it is also how cow's milk (a key allergen) is first given.
notes.Cheese: A first food; also a way to give cow's milk (a key allergen).
notes.A taste: How much of a solid meal the baby ate.
notes.A few spoons: How much of a solid meal the baby ate.
notes.A small bowl: How much of a solid meal the baby ate.
notes.How much: Label above how much of a solid meal was eaten.
notes.Not yet: Heading: foods not to give a baby yet.
notes.Time for solid foods: Title of the sheet shown the month a child turns 6 months old.
notes.Mark an allergy: Button and title: record that the child is allergic to a food.
notes.Which food?: In the allergy form: which food the child reacted to.
notes.Choose the food: Message: no food was chosen in the allergy form.
notes.Remove {food} from {name}'s allergies?: {food} is a food, {name} a child's name.
notes.Log a first food: Button: open the feed form to log a first solid food.
notes.Foods tried (first time): PDF report: each food given so far, with the day it was first given.
notes.Family tree: Heading in the Family tab: every family log the person is in (their own, and the children they look after, e.g. a sister's), drawn as a small tree. Also the button that opens it and a tour step.
notes.Your family: In the family tree: the family log this person is a parent in.
notes.{names}'s family: In the family tree: another family, named after its parents, e.g. "Sarah's family" or "Sarah and Tom's family" ({names} is one name or a list of names).
notes.Add a family: Button and sheet title in the family tree: join another family's log (for example to look after a sister's children) by scanning an invite from one of its parents.
notes.You're in: {family}: Short message when a request to join another family was approved; {family} is its name in the family tree.
notes.{n} change not sent yet: it goes when yo: In the family tree, on a family kept on the phone that has changes made offline that have not reached the server yet.
notes.Switching…: On a button while the app switches to another family's log.
notes.Now showing {family}: Short message after switching to another family's log.
notes.Could not switch: {reason}: Short message when switching to another family's log failed; {reason} says why.
notes.Switch family: Title of the sheet (and the spoken label of the button at the top of the screen) for choosing which family's log is shown.
notes.Open: Button in the family tree: show this family's log.
notes.asked to join {family} as **{role}**: Under a request to join another of the parent's family logs; {family} is its name in the family tree, {role} a role such as Caregiver.
notes.Medical assistant: A role in the family log: a nurse, a home health aide or similar who helps with the baby. Shown next to people's names.
notes.Moved away: A reason for retiring a helper (a caregiver, babysitter or medical assistant who no longer helps).
notes.No longer helps: A reason for retiring a helper: they stopped doing the work.
notes.Passed away: A reason for retiring a helper: they died. Use the gentle, respectful wording.
notes.Family: {names}: In the family tree, under a family: its relatives (parents and family members), e.g. "Family: Dad and Gran".
notes.Families you help with: Heading in the Family tab: the families this person looks after as a caregiver, babysitter, medical assistant or friend (not a relative), listed apart from the family tree.
notes.Retire: Button for a parent: mark a caregiver, babysitter, medical assistant or friend as no longer helping (they moved away, stopped, or died). Their access ends; a note of them stays.
notes.Retired ({n}): Heading of a twirl-down list of the helpers who were retired, with how many there are.
notes.Caregivers and helpers: Heading in the Family tab: the caregivers, babysitters, medical assistants and friends of the family shown, listed apart from its family. Also a tour step.
notes.No caregivers, babysitters or medical as: Shown when the list of caregivers and helpers is empty.
notes.retired {date}: On the Retired list, after a person's role: when they were retired, e.g. "Babysitter · retired Mar 3, 2026 · Moved away".
notes.Retire {name}: Title of the sheet for retiring a caregiver, babysitter, medical assistant or friend.
notes.Why (optional): Label above the reasons for retiring someone (Moved away, No longer helps, Passed away, Other).
notes.{name} is retired: Short message after a parent retired a helper.
On a retired helper's card, when they never added contact details.
notes.Remove from the list: Button on a retired helper's card: delete the note about them from the Retired list.
notes.Remove {name} from the Retired list? The: Question before deleting the note about a retired helper.
notes.{actor} retired {person}: A line of the activity log: a parent retired a helper.
notes.Families and relatives: Title of the twirl-down (fold-out) list under the family tree picture: every family log you are family in, with its children and relatives. Also a tour step title.
notes.{n} year: A child's age on the family tree, in whole years (from two years old). Like '{n} month' and '{n} week'.
notes.Open {family}: Button (and screen-reader label on the family tree picture): show that family's log in the app. {family} is its name, e.g. "Sarah's family".
notes.Show {name}'s day: Button on a child's card, opened by tapping the child on the family tree: show that child's Day page (switching to their family first). {name} is the child's name.
notes.{n} waiting for your approval: Under the title of the families list (folded up): how many people asked to join one of the families you are a parent in; their requests are inside the list.
notes.Your children's family tree: their paren: Tour of the Family tab: the picture of the children's family tree. 'The +' = the round buds with a plus where a parent can add someone.
notes.Grandparent: On the children's family tree (Family tab): a picture of a storybook tree with the children on the grass at the foot of the trunk, their parents where it forks, aunts and uncles beside them, grandparents and great-grandparents above. Relations are the children's: 'Grandparent' = the children's grandparent. Who someone is to the children; also the label under an empty bud where one can be added. Short, one word if the language has a neutral one.
notes.Great-grandparent: On the children's family tree (Family tab): a picture of a storybook tree with the children on the grass at the foot of the trunk, their parents where it forks, aunts and uncles beside them, grandparents and great-grandparents above. Relations are the children's: 'Grandparent' = the children's grandparent. Who someone is to the children (a grandparent's parent); also read out for an empty bud. As short as the language allows.
notes.Aunt or uncle: On the children's family tree (Family tab): a picture of a storybook tree with the children on the grass at the foot of the trunk, their parents where it forks, aunts and uncles beside them, grandparents and great-grandparents above. Relations are the children's: 'Grandparent' = the children's grandparent. A parent's brother or sister, or their partner; also the label under an empty bud. Short: no more than about 14 letters if possible.
notes.Cousin: On the children's family tree (Family tab): a picture of a storybook tree with the children on the grass at the foot of the trunk, their parents where it forks, aunts and uncles beside them, grandparents and great-grandparents above. Relations are the children's: 'Grandparent' = the children's grandparent. An aunt or uncle's child.
notes.Add the children's other parent: On the children's family tree (Family tab): a picture of a storybook tree with the children on the grass at the foot of the trunk, their parents where it forks, aunts and uncles beside them, grandparents and great-grandparents above. Relations are the children's: 'Grandparent' = the children's grandparent. What tapping the bud next to a parent does (screen readers read it), and the title of the sheet.
notes.Add a grandparent: On the children's family tree (Family tab): a picture of a storybook tree with the children on the grass at the foot of the trunk, their parents where it forks, aunts and uncles beside them, grandparents and great-grandparents above. Relations are the children's: 'Grandparent' = the children's grandparent. Title of the sheet (and what the bud does).
notes.Add a great-grandparent: On the children's family tree (Family tab): a picture of a storybook tree with the children on the grass at the foot of the trunk, their parents where it forks, aunts and uncles beside them, grandparents and great-grandparents above. Relations are the children's: 'Grandparent' = the children's grandparent. Title of the sheet (and what the bud does).
notes.Add an aunt or uncle: On the children's family tree (Family tab): a picture of a storybook tree with the children on the grass at the foot of the trunk, their parents where it forks, aunts and uncles beside them, grandparents and great-grandparents above. Relations are the children's: 'Grandparent' = the children's grandparent. Title of the sheet (and what the bud does).
notes.Add a partner: Button on an aunt or uncle's card on the family tree: add their husband, wife or partner.
notes.Add a cousin: Button on an aunt or uncle's card on the family tree: add one of their children (the children's cousin).
notes.{name}'s parent: Under the title of the sheet that adds someone to the family tree: who they are. {name} is the person they are the mother or father of.
notes.{name}'s brother or sister: Under the title of the sheet that adds an aunt or uncle to the family tree. {name} is the children's parent whose sibling they are.
notes.{name}'s partner: Under the title of the sheet that adds an aunt or uncle's husband, wife or partner.
notes.{name}'s child: Under the title of the sheet that adds a cousin: whose child they are.
notes.Tap a + to add grandparents, great-grand: Under the family tree picture, for a parent, while it has only the parents and children. '+' = the round buds with a plus.
notes.A parent can add grandparents, aunts, un: Under the family tree picture, for a family member (who can't change it), while it has only the parents and children.
notes.{name}'s side: On someone's card from the family tree: which side of the family they are on. {name} is one of the children's parents, e.g. 'Grandparent · Jo's side'.
notes.What the children call them: Label of a field (and on someone's card) on the family tree: the name the children use for this person, e.g. Nana, Grandpa Joe, Auntie Sue.
notes.In loving memory: A tick box on the family tree sheet, and a line on someone's card: this relative has died. Gentle and respectful.
notes.Already in Little Log: Above a list of people who use the app (in this family or a relative's), to pick one instead of typing a name, when adding someone to the family tree.
notes.e.g. Nana, Grandpa Joe: Example in the field 'What the children call them'. Use names children in your language would use for grandparents.
notes.Remove from the tree: Red button on the sheet that changes someone on the family tree.
notes.Remove {name} from the family tree? Anyo: Question before taking someone off the family tree: their parents, partner and children on the tree are removed with them.
notes.{actor} changed the family tree: A line of the activity log (parents only).
notes.The family tree changed meanwhile: try a: Message when someone else changed the family tree at the same time and the place you were adding to is gone.
notes.English oak: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (Quercus robur, the common oak of Britain and Ireland.)
notes.Red maple: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (Acer rubrum, North America's most common tree.)
notes.European beech: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (Fagus sylvatica.)
notes.Silver birch: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (Betula pendula, white bark.)
notes.Olive tree: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language.
notes.Eucalyptus: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (the gum tree of Australia.)
notes.Cherry blossom: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (the flowering cherry, sakura.)
notes.Banyan: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (Ficus benghalensis, with roots hanging from its branches.)
notes.Mango tree: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language.
notes.Umbrella acacia: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (Vachellia tortilis, the flat-topped tree of the African savanna.)
notes.Jacaranda: A kind of tree, for the children's family tree (a soft watercolour painting): the family's tree is the kind that grows most where the family comes from. Use the everyday name people use for this tree in your language. (Jacaranda mimosifolia, purple flowers.)
notes.North America: Where this kind of tree is the most common one: shown next to the tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple · North America'. Short.
notes.Central Europe: Where this kind of tree is the most common one: shown next to the tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple · North America'. Short.
notes.Northern and Eastern Europe: Where this kind of tree is the most common one: shown next to the tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple · North America'. Short.
notes.The Mediterranean and the Middle East: Where this kind of tree is the most common one: shown next to the tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple · North America'. Short.
notes.East Asia: Where this kind of tree is the most common one: shown next to the tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple · North America'. Short.
notes.South Asia: Where this kind of tree is the most common one: shown next to the tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple · North America'. Short.
notes.Southeast Asia: Where this kind of tree is the most common one: shown next to the tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple · North America'. Short.
notes.Africa: Where this kind of tree is the most common one: shown next to the tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple · North America'. Short.
notes.Change tree: Small button under the family tree (parents only): choose another kind of tree for the painting.
notes.Your family's tree: Title of the sheet where a parent picks the kind of tree the family tree is painted as.
notes.Pick the tree that grows most where your: On the sheet where a parent picks the kind of tree for the family tree.
notes.Automatic: {tree}: The first choice on that sheet: the tree picked for where this phone is (its region and language). {tree} is a tree's name, e.g. 'Red maple'.
notes.Meal: A kind of entry and its button, from a year old: a meal a child ate (breakfast, lunch, dinner or a snack). One short word.
notes.meal: Fills {what} in "Add {what}" / "Edit {what}" (Add meal), and lists of kinds of entry.
notes.Potty: A kind of entry and its button, for potty training: a toddler using the potty (a small toilet for young children). Also one of the answers to "Where?": on the potty (not the toilet). One short word.
notes.potty: Fills {what} in "Add {what}" / "Edit {what}" (Add potty), and lists of kinds of entry.
notes.Big moment: A first or a day to remember in a child's life (first smile, first steps, first day of school), saved in the app's journal. Also a calendar legend.
notes.big moment: Lower-case form of "Big moment", in lists of kinds of entry.
notes.milk: Fills {what} in "Add {what}" / "Edit {what}" for a toddler's drink of milk (Add milk).
notes.cup: How the milk was drunk: from a cup (the other choices are breast and bottle). Lower case, like "breast" and "bottle".
notes.Cup: A drink of milk from a cup (no amount given).
notes.Cup {ml} ml: A drink of milk from a cup, with how much: {ml} is a number.
notes.Cup, bottle or breast?: Travel mode's quick sheet: how a toddler had their milk.
notes.Cow's milk: Plain milk from cows, as a drink for a child over 1.
notes.Plant milk: Milk made from plants: oat, soy, almond…
notes.Breakfast: One of the meals of the day.
notes.Lunch: One of the meals of the day.
notes.Hardly any: How much of a meal a child ate: almost nothing.
notes.Some: How much of a meal a child ate: some of it.
notes.Most: How much of a meal a child ate: most of it.
notes.All of it: How much of a meal a child ate: all of it.
notes.Nothing yet: Potty: the child sat on the potty, but nothing came (yet).
notes.Stayed dry: Potty training: the child's diaper or pants were found dry (a success).
notes.Toilet: On the (grown-ups') toilet, rather than the potty.
notes.Accident: Potty training: the child wet or soiled their pants instead of using the potty.
notes.Accident: {what}: {what} is Pee, Poo or Pee + Poo.
notes.asked to go: The child asked to use the potty by themselves (shown after where they went).
notes.Asked to go: The child asked to use the potty by themselves. A tick box, and a row in the stats.
notes.{n} on the potty: How many times a child peed or pooed in the potty in a day.
notes.on the potty: A chart's series: times in the potty.
notes.Meals: A group of entries, a stats card and a tile: an older child's meals.
notes.Meals & milk: A group of entries: a toddler's meals and drinks of milk.
notes.Feeding & meals: A group of entries on a page with a baby and an older child: a baby's feeds and an older child's meals.
notes.Diapers & potty: A group of entries: diapers and the potty.
notes.big moment: {what}: Read out by screen readers on a calendar day that has a big moment. {what} is its name, like "First steps".
notes.More: {list}: Travel mode's button for the other kinds of entry; {list} is their buttons' names with dots between them, like "Potty · Health · Meds · Night wake".
notes.{years} {months}: A child's age, like "2 years 3 months": {years} is "2 years" and {months} is "3 months" (both already translated). Reorder them, or add a word between them, if your language needs it.
notes.Newborn: A stage of life: the first 3 months. A heading in the journal of big moments.
notes.Toddler: A stage of life: from 1 to 3 years. A heading in the journal of big moments.
notes.Preschooler: A stage of life: from 3 years until school starts. A heading in the journal of big moments.
notes.School age: A stage of life: from starting school to 12. A heading in the journal of big moments.
notes.Teenager: A stage of life: from 12 to 18. A heading in the journal of big moments.
notes.Grown up: A stage of life: 18 and over. A heading in the journal of big moments.
notes.Born: A big moment: the day the child was born. The big moments are short captions, like in a photo album, with the child as the one who did it.
notes.Birthday: A big moment: a birthday (the app shows how old the child turned next to it).
notes.Big-kid bed: A big moment: moving from a crib (cot) to an ordinary bed.
notes.Goodbye pacifier: A big moment: the child stopped using a pacifier (a dummy, a soother).
notes.Last bottle: A big moment: the last time the child drank from a baby bottle.
notes.Swam without floaties: A big moment: swimming without arm-band floats.
notes.Rode a bike without training wheels: A big moment: riding a bicycle without stabilisers.
notes.First day at secondary school: A big moment: the first day at the next school after primary school (middle school, high school).
notes.Prom or formal: A big moment: the dance or ball at the end of school.
notes.Graduated: A big moment: finished school (or university).
notes.Cord stump fell off: A big moment: the umbilical cord stump fell off.
notes.First show or recital: A big moment: the first time on stage (a school play, a dance or music show).
notes.Started a new school year: A big moment: the first day of a new school year (every year).
notes.Out of diapers in the day: A big moment: the child no longer wears diapers in the daytime.
notes.Dry at night: A big moment: the child stays dry all night without a diaper.
notes.Save a big moment: A button and a sheet title: to save a new big moment in the journal.
notes.Ideas for other ages: A fold-out list of ideas of big moments for younger and older children.
notes.e.g. First time at the beach: An example of a big moment written in your own words.
notes.Latest big moments: On the family tree: a child's most recent big moments.
notes.Toddlers and preschoolers: A section of the Guide: children from 1 to 5 years old.
notes.Toddler sleep: A topic of the Guide: how much toddlers sleep, naps, moving to a bed.
notes.Screens: A topic of the Guide: screen time (phones, tablets, TV).
notes.Picky eating: A topic of the Guide: toddlers who refuse foods or eat little.
notes.Vaccine: A kind of entry in the health record: a dose of a vaccine (a vaccination, a jab, a shot).
notes.Doctor visit: A kind of entry in the health record: a checkup, a visit to the dentist, a time the child was seen when unwell, …
notes.Growth: A kind of entry in the health record (a measurement of weight, length or height and head size), and the heading of the growth section.
notes.measurement: Fills {what} in "Add {what}" / "Edit {what}" (Add measurement): a weight, length or head size measured.
notes.Measurement: An entry with weight, length or head size, when none of them is shown.
notes.Unwell: A kind of doctor visit: the child was seen because they were ill.
notes.Eyes: A kind of doctor visit: an eye test.
notes.Hearing: A kind of doctor visit: a hearing test.
notes.Specialist: A kind of doctor visit: a specialist doctor.
notes.Hospital: A kind of doctor visit: a stay or a visit at the hospital.
notes.Urgent care or ER: A kind of doctor visit: an urgent care clinic or the emergency room (A&E).
notes.{n} in: A length in inches ("in" is the unit, not the word "in").
notes.in: The unit inches (2.54 cm), as a short label on a chart and next to a field. Not the word "in".
notes.lb: The unit pounds (weight), as a short label.
notes.oz: The unit ounces (weight), as a short label.
notes.kg: The unit kilograms, as a short label.
notes.cm: The unit centimetres, as a short label.
notes.{lb} lb {oz} oz: A weight in pounds and ounces, like "27 lb 5 oz".
notes.dose {n}: The nth dose of a vaccine: dose 1, dose 2 …
notes.head {size}: A head measurement (head circumference): {size} is like "46 cm".
notes.Head: Head size (the head circumference) of a baby or toddler: a measurement and a table column.
notes.Weight: A child's weight: a measurement and a table column.
notes.Length or height: A child's length (lying down, for a baby) or height (standing): a measurement and a table column.
notes.BMI: Body mass index. Use your language's usual abbreviation.
notes.Age: A table column: how old the child was at a measurement.
notes.Who: A table column: the doctor or the clinic.
notes.Where: A table column: where a vaccine was given.
notes.Visit: A table column: the kind of doctor visit.
notes.percentile {n}: Where a measurement falls on the growth charts: {n} is a whole number from 1 to 99. Say it the way your language says "the 55th percentile" (one form that works for every number).
notes.{n} for the health record: How many of the day's entries went into the health record (vaccines, doctor visits, measurements).
notes.Health record: A child's health record: vaccines, doctor visits and measurements of growth. A button and a page.
notes.Health checks: A section of the Guide: vaccines, checkups and growth charts.
notes.Units: A setting: kilograms and centimetres, or pounds and inches.
notes.Hib: A vaccine (Haemophilus influenzae type b). Keep the abbreviation if your country uses it.
notes.MenB: A vaccine (meningococcal group B). Use the abbreviation your country uses.
notes.MenC: A vaccine (meningococcal group C). Use the abbreviation your country uses.
notes.MenACWY: A vaccine (meningococcal groups A, C, W and Y). Use the abbreviation your country uses.
notes.RSV: A vaccine or antibody against respiratory syncytial virus. Use the abbreviation your country uses (VRS in French and Spanish …).
notes.HPV: A vaccine against human papillomavirus. Use the abbreviation your country uses.
notes.6-in-1 (diphtheria, tetanus, whooping co: The combined vaccine given to babies (hexavalent). Use the name parents know it by where your language is spoken.
notes.Activity log: Heading and sheet: the log of who added, changed or deleted what.
notes.Daycare & school: A group of entries and a stats card: when a child was dropped off at daycare, preschool, school or wherever they are looked after, and picked up.
notes.Drop-off: A kind of entry and its button: the child was dropped off at daycare, preschool, school, a childminder's… One or two short words.
notes.Pick-up: A kind of entry: the child was picked up from daycare, preschool, school…
notes.Homework: A kind of entry and its button for a school child: homework, reading or practising (an instrument, a sport); also the first of those kinds.
notes.Reading: A kind of homework: reading (a school book, reading practice).
notes.Practising: A kind of homework: practising an instrument or a sport at home.
notes.Playing outside: A kind of play or activity.
notes.Reading together: A kind of play for a toddler or preschooler: reading books together.
notes.Swimming: A kind of play or activity (swimming, swimming lessons).
notes.Music: A kind of play or activity (music, a music lesson).
notes.Art or crafts: A kind of play or activity: drawing, painting, crafts.
notes.Sport: A kind of activity for a school child: sport, a team or a sports club.
notes.Dance: A kind of activity for a school child: dance, a dance class.
notes.Games: A kind of activity for a school child: games (board games, video games).
notes.Club or group: A kind of activity for a school child: a club, scouts or guides, a youth group.
notes.dropped off by {name}: Under a drop-off in the list: who dropped the child off. {name} is a person's name.
notes.Picked up from {place}: A pick-up in the list. {place} is where: Daycare, Preschool, School, a childminder's… (or a place typed in).
notes.Picked up: A button in the banner (tap when the child has been picked up), and a pick-up in the list when no place is known.
notes.by {name}: Under a pick-up in the list: who picked the child up.
notes.School: The group of entries and the stats card for a school child (drop-offs and pick-ups at school); also a place a child is dropped off at.
notes.Activities & homework: A group of entries for a school child: activities and homework.
notes.Play & homework: A group of entries on a page with a school child and a younger one: play, activities and homework.
notes.{name} picks up at {time}: The plan for the day, shown to the family: who will pick the child up, and when. {name} is a person's name, {time} a time like 3:15 PM.
notes.{name} picks up: The plan for the day: who will pick the child up.
notes.pick-up at {time}: The plan for the day: when the child will be picked up.
notes.{name} is at school age: Drop-off and Ho: A note at the top of the Day page when a child reaches school age. {name} is one or more names; Drop-off and Homework are the buttons' names, as you translated them.
notes.{name} picked up: Title of the sheet that logs a pick-up. {name} is the child.
notes.At {place} since {time}: In the banner at the top while the child is at daycare or school: {place} is the place (Preschool, School…), {time} when they were dropped off.
notes.Who picked up?: In the pick-up sheet: who picked the child up.
notes.Someone else: An option: a person not in the list (their name is typed in).
notes.{n} pick-up: How many pick-ups in a day (in the summary of the day's group).
notes.Activities: A stats card for a school child: activities.
notes.Activities per day: A row of the stats card: time spent on activities per day.
notes.Days there: A row of the Daycare & school stats card: on how many days the child was there.
notes.Time there on those days: A row of the Daycare & school stats card: how long the child was there, on average, on the days they went.
notes.hours there: Series name in a chart: hours at daycare or school per day.
notes.Homework per day: A row of the Homework stats card.
notes.every day: How often a time in the routine comes back: every day of the week.
notes.Other days of the week: A heading on the Routine tab: the times that come back on other days of the week (school on a Monday, swimming on Tuesdays).
notes.Daycare, school, homework, and lessons a: A note on the Routine tab.
notes.Where?: In the drop-off sheet: where the child was dropped off.
notes.From where?: In the pick-up sheet: where the child was picked up from.
notes.Name of the place: A field: the name of a place typed in (where the child was dropped off).
notes.Dropped off by (optional): A field in the drop-off sheet: who dropped the child off.
notes.Picked up by (optional): A field in the pick-up sheet: who picked the child up.
notes.Who picks up? (optional): A field in the drop-off sheet: who will pick the child up later.
notes.e.g. Grandpa: An example name for who picks the child up: your language's everyday word for a grandfather.
notes.Pick-up time (optional): A field in the drop-off sheet: when the child will be picked up.
notes.Already picked up? (optional): A field in the drop-off sheet, for a day logged afterwards: when the child was picked up.
notes.What?: In the homework sheet: homework, reading or practising.
notes.Subject (optional): A field in the homework sheet: the school subject.
notes.Pages read (optional): A field in the homework sheet, for reading.
notes.Choose where: An error: no place was chosen for a drop-off or a pick-up.
notes.Daycare: A place a child is dropped off at: a nursery or day care centre for babies and toddlers.
notes.Preschool: A place a child is dropped off at: preschool, kindergarten or nursery school, from about 3 years old.
notes.Childminder: A place a child is dropped off at: a childminder (someone who looks after children in their own home).
notes.Grandparents: A place a child is dropped off at: the grandparents' home.
notes.After-school club: A place a child is dropped off at: an after-school club or after-school care.
notes.Friend's house: A place a child is dropped off at: a friend's house.
notes.Teeth: A topic of the Guide for school children: teeth and the dentist.
notes.Out and about: A topic of the Guide for school children: safety on bikes and scooters, in the car, near water and crossing roads.
notes.Bedwetting: A topic of the Guide: wetting the bed at night.
notes.Worries and feelings: A topic of the Guide: a child's worries, anxiety and mood.
